SFU
Self-supervised confidence-aware denoising imputation of genomic data
Mehdi Foroozandeh, Abdul Rahman Diab, and Maxwell Libbrecht
mehdiforoozandeh.github.io/CANDI

The problem

Most (cell type, assay) experiments were never run, and those that were differ in depth, read length, run type and platform. In the ENCODE Imputation Challenge, a baseline that averages each assay over other cell types beat all but two submitted methods [1].

CANDI

Confidence-Aware Neural Denoising Imputer [2] is a self-supervised transformer over raw read counts, DNA sequence and four experimental covariates. It predicts a distribution for every assay in every 25 bp bin, so each imputed value has an interval. It has no cell-type embedding, so it runs on cell types it has never seen.

Key findings

  • CANDI is 1st of 26 on the ENCODE Imputation Challenge blind test.
  • CANDI's intervals are calibrated, and its latent features are predictive of gene expression.

CANDI schematic workflow

Top: one cell type is sliced out of the cell type × assay × genome tensor, and a 30 kb window of it goes into CANDI as raw counts, DNA and covariates. Grey assays were never measured; yellow ones are masked in training. Bottom: CANDI returns a mean and a 95% interval for every assay, and window by window this fills every missing thread of the tensor.

Downstream utility of CANDI

[1] Schreiber J, Boix C, et al. The ENCODE Imputation Challenge: a critical assessment of methods for cross-cell type imputation of epigenomic profiles. Genome Biol 24:79 (2023).

[2] Foroozandeh M, Diab AR, Libbrecht M. CANDI: self-supervised, confidence-aware denoising imputation of genomic data. bioRxiv 2025.01.23.634626 (2025).

Panels C–D: blind-test scoring from the Libbrecht lab's EIC reproduction (experiments 017, 025). Baseline is the challenge's average-activity track. The output correction was chosen after the challenge results were public; none of its numbers is fitted on blind-test data.

Fixing the signal-level shift in the ENCODE Imputation Challenge blind test

51 blind-test experiments (12 cell types, 8 assays), scored with the challenge's own nine measures and ranking statistic; our scorer reproduces every published entry to a median relative difference of 9 × 10−10. CANDI's output as it comes ranks 14th, so for each assay we pass it through one fixed layer, max(β0 + β1·CANDI + β2·baseline, 0), whose 24 numbers are fitted by least squares on the 133 training experiments only; with it, CANDI ranks 1st.
